summary: Red-brick light on Harbor Point, lit in 1884 and kept by Elizabeth Whitney Williams for 29 years; replaced by a steel light on the point in 1963.

lens.where: original lens still mounted in the 1884 tower (Rowlett)

structures.type: square brick tower attached to keeper's house
structures.note: Height given as 10.4 m in the record; Rowlett gives 40 ft (12 m); see resolved conflicts

structures.type: square pyramidal frame tower on brick piers

structures.note: Height disputed: Rowlett 72 ft (22 m); Lighthouse Friends 41 ft

access.note: Harbor Point is a gated community run by the Harbor Point Association, which owns the lighthouse. Grounds and tower generally closed.

visit.note: Guided tours reported as infrequent (once or twice a year per Rowlett; once every three years per Lighthouse Friends)

facts.agency: Harbor Point Association (owner of the 1884 light, per Rowlett and Lighthouse Friends)

events.note: Red-brick tower and attached keeper's house finished 18 September 1884
Lamp first lit 25 September 1884 (memoir and Lighthouse Friends agree)
Fourth-order Fresnel lens showing a fixed red light, 41 ft focal plane
Summer kitchen built (fiscal year ended June 30, 1894)
Fog bell and two-story pyramidal bell tower set up on 1 June 1896
Alfred Curtis Erickson became principal keeper after Williams left
Keeper towed a disabled launch to safety (bulletin index)
Keeper rescued a woman who fell out of a boat near the station, 4 September (1917 bulletin). Lighthouse Friends dates a rescue of a woman from a boat to 1918; not stated whether the same event.
Six men picked up from the burning launch Evelyn (Lighthouse Friends)
Coast Guard public hearing on discontinuing the light and its fog bell
Steel skeletal light erected on the point with a green flash
Brick light discontinued; property exchanged with the Harbor Point Association

corrections.why: 21.9 m (72 ft) is the 1963 steel light (Rowlett). The 1884 brick light had a focal plane of 41 ft, about 12.5 m (Lighthouse Friends).
Fl G 6s is the green flash of the 1963 steel light (Rowlett). The original brick light showed a fixed red light (Lighthouse Friends).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record gives 10.4 m. Rowlett gives 40 ft (12 m) for the square brick tower; this was not checked against the USLHS structure data and should be reviewed.
Rowlett gives a 72-foot (22 m) steel tower; Lighthouse Friends gives 41 feet. The story reports the disagreement.
Rowlett says guided tours were held once or twice a year in recent years; Lighthouse Friends says the historical society gives tours roughly once every three years. Reported as a disagreement.
Lighthouse Friends says the lens was installed in the 1884 tower; no lens manufacture date is given in the sources read. Not resolved; not in the story.

The 1917 Lighthouse Service Bulletin (PDF p. 44) dates Erickson's rescue of a woman who fell out of a boat to 4 September 1917. Lighthouse Friends dates a rescue of a woman from a boat to 1918. The story reports the bulletin date and notes the LF date; it does not say they are the same event.
Lighthouse Friends gives the parcel the Coast Guard received as a fifty-foot-square parcel owned by the Harbor Point Association; the story now says so, instead of 'a smaller parcel'.

notes_for_editor:
1. The 1884 brick light is inactive; the record's active characteristic (Fl G 6s) and focal height (21.9 m) describe the 1963 steel light. See corrections.
2. Elizabeth Whitney Williams is printed 'Elizabeth Whitney Williams' on the USLHS roster and 'Elizabeth Van Riper Williams' in Lighthouse Friends' head-keeper line. Her memoir gives 'Mrs. Daniel Williams' as her official title from 1876. The story uses the roster name and the memoir title.
3. The memoir (Gutenberg #34769, from the University of Michigan Making of America scan, copyright 1905) is cited by its printed page numbers, which the Gutenberg transcription marks as [Pg n]. The Beaver Island passages about her first husband's death and her own appointment are her account; the dates and the Beaver Island keeper line are from Lighthouse Friends. The Lighthouse Board volumes for 1869-1872 are not in the corpus, so those dates are not checked in a primary source.
4. The 1915 tow is cited to the Bulletin index entry; the Bulletin text for 1915 was not located.
5. Lighthouse Friends is all-rights-reserved and was used for facts only, with prose written here; its one quotation is Poe's 1871 sentence as the page gives it.
6. The 1923 Evelyn fire comes from Lighthouse Friends alone; it is marked as such in the story. Check it against the Coast Guard or Commissioner records before publication.
7. Keeper spans and roles come from the USLHS roster (NARA registers via Kraig Anderson's inventory), not checked against the NARA registers.
8. Harbor Point is private property. The story says the light is not open to casual visitors and gives the tour information the sources report.
9. Wikipedia was consulted for leads only and is not cited for any fact.
